sentences.text:
This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 02.07.2005 passed by the Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 38/2002, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The date of accident, the issue of negligence, and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality and are not under challenge in the present appeal.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, considering the injuries sustained by Bhagwan Das, the claimant, in the motor accident, compensation to the tune of 17,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization was awarded.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Award, the appellant/claimant has preferred the present appeal contending that the learned Claims Tribunal passed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4517 2 MA-1041-2005 the Award without proper appreciation of law and evidence and that the compensation awarded is on the lower side.

It is contended by learned counsel for the appellant that the oral and documentary evidence produced on record clearly establishes that prior to the accident, the appellant was a healthy person aged about 26 years and was working as an agriculturist as well as a labourer, earning approximately 4,000/- per month.
It is further Bhagwan Das vs Satish Sharma And Anr.

1 submitted that due to the accident, the appellant sustained grievous injuries and suffered severe physical and mental pain during the course of treatment, incurred substantial medical expenses,
and has been rendered incapable of pursuing his vocation for the rest of his life.

It is further contended that the Claims Tribunal committed a grave legal error in not accepting the appellant's claim of permanent disability allegedly resulting from serious head injuries sustained in the accident.

According to the appellant, the documentary and oral evidence, including the permanent disability certificate, fully establishes the factum of permanent disability, and no rebuttal evidence was led by the respondents nor were the appellant's witnesses effectively cross- examined.

On these grounds, enhancement of compensation under various heads, including permanent disability, loss of income, pain and suffering, medical expenses, and loss of amenities of life, has been prayed for.
None appeared for the respondents, though they were duly served.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.

Upon careful perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal as well as the permanent disability certificate (Ex.P-35), it is evident that Dr. Yogendra Pradhan, who issued the said certificate, has not elaborated the basis or reasoning as to how and in what manner the claimant suffered permanent disability.

The Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4517 3 MA-1041-2005 Tribunal, after considering all aspects of the disability certificate and the evidence of Dr. Pradhan,
has rightly discarded the claim of permanent disability, as discussed in detail in paragraph 8 of the impugned Award.
This Court finds no infirmity, illegality, or perversity in the said finding.
Accordingly, the contention of the appellant regarding permanent disability is rejected.

So far as the contention regarding enhancement of compensation is concerned, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, and more particularly considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident, this Court deems it appropriate to enhance the compensation by a lump sum amount of 25,000/-.
Accordingly, the present appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation is enhanced by a lump sum amount of 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty-Five Thousand Only), in addition to the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
The present appeal stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
